title: GAE, its lambda limits, and truncation done right
brief: Compute generalized advantage estimates by backward recursion, recover the TD error and the Monte Carlo advantage as its two limits, and bootstrap correctly when a time limit cuts an episode off.
hints: Only terminated removes the bootstrap from delta. A truncated step still adds gamma * next_values[t].
Both flags stop the recursion: multiply the carried advantage by (1 - (terminated | truncated)) before adding it to delta.
Loop t from T - 1 down to 0 with a running value initialized to zeros of shape delta.shape[1:]. That handles (T,) and (T, N) in one piece of code.
In next_state_values, shift values left by one, put last_value at the end, then use np.where(done, final_values, shifted).
